_note: Emitted by build.py as dist/_headers, which Netlify picks up automatically — the same pattern redirects.json already uses for dist/_redirects. These deliberately do NOT live in netlify.toml: its header parser silently dropped Content-Security-Policy and Permissions-Policy (values containing '=' and ';'), reporting 'header rules processed without errors' while serving neither. Verified on deploy preview #2. Order matters: '/*' comes first, and the narrower asset rules after it override Cache-Control.

_csp.why: Every origin was inventoried from the built output, not guessed. Do not loosen this to add a tracker without asking.
_csp.script-src: One inline script in base.html sets the .js class. It is pinned by SHA-256 so 'unsafe-inline' is not needed. If that line is ever edited the hash must be regenerated, or the reveal animations stop working and content stays hidden.
_csp.style-src: 'unsafe-inline' is required — the pages use style= attributes, which cannot be hashed.
_csp.img-src: data: covers the 43-byte transparent GIF the hero falls back to on mobile. i.ytimg.com serves YouTube thumbnails.
_csp.frame-src: youtube-nocookie is the click-to-load player; openstreetmap is the map on /contact/.
_csp.form-action: 'self' only. Booking enquiries post to our own /thanks/ via Netlify Forms, so nothing should ever post off-site.

values.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-qOhFsq0QMV2REqNwk5hGH5bZE9SkX6gt6yeyKdYPv+U='; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https://i.ytimg.com; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://www.youtube.com https://www.openstreetmap.org; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests
